t: The Secretary shall designate ports of documentation in the United States where vessels may be documented and instruments affecting title to, or interest in, documented vessels may be recorded. The Secretary shall specify the geographic area to be served by each designated port, and he may discontinue, relocate, or designate additional ports of documentation.

fable.w: The section gives the Secretary unilateral authority to designate, relocate, or discontinue ports of documentation and to specify the areas they serve. The tempting reading is that vessel owners documenting vessels or recording instruments are participating, but that is akin to an application or filing, not involvement in a federal decision. No consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking requirement, or right to sue is mentioned.
fable.s: The Secretary shall designate ports of documentation in the United States where vessels may be documented and instruments affecting title to, or interest in, documented vessels may be recorded.

opus.w: The Secretary alone designates, relocates, or discontinues ports of documentation. The section does not require consulting outside parties, a public comment period, a hearing, an advisory body, or rulemaking. Calling this administrative decision participation would be the wrong reading, because no one outside the federal government is brought into the decision.
opus.s: The Secretary shall specify the geographic area to be served by each designated port, and he may discontinue, relocate, or designate additional ports of documentation.
opus.b:
1. **Analysis.** One could read this as "Yes" because the Secretary designates ports and service areas, which looks like formal administrative decision-making, close to rulemaking. That reading doesn't hold up. The text says nothing about issuing regulations, holding a comment period or hearing, consulting states or industry, or giving anyone a right to object or sue. The Secretary acts alone, so no one outside the federal government takes part.

2. **Label.**

qwen_chat.w: This section grants the Secretary of Commerce (or relevant Secretary) the unilateral authority to designate, relocate, or discontinue ports of documentation. It does not require or recommend consultation with any outside parties such as state governments, local authorities, or the public. The decision-making process described is entirely internal to the federal executive branch.
qwen_chat.s: The Secretary shall designate ports of documentation in the United States where vessels may be documented and instruments affecting title to, or interest in, documented vessels may be recorded. The Secretary shall specify the geographic area to be served by each designated port, and he may discontinue, relocate, or designate additional ports of documentation.
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might argue that "designating ports" involves consultation with local port authorities or the public, but the text does not mention any such consultation. It simply grants the Secretary the authority to make these designations. The actors involved are solely the Secretary (federal official) and the ports (locations/federal administrative units). There is no mention of outside parties (states, tribes, public, companies) being consulted or participating in the decision.
